sentences.text: 1. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., 1973 seeking quashing of FIR No. 342/2019 dated 17.07.2019 under Sections 498A/406/34, IPC, registered at Police Station Dwarka South, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom, on the grounds of settlement between the parties.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the parties submit that the dispute between the parties have been resolved and the terms of settlement have been reduced into writing vide Memorandum of This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 00:08:32 Understanding (MOU) dated 01.11.2021.

Notarized copy of the MOU was subsequently filed by the petitioner under the cover of Index No. 1403421 dated 10.08.2023.
3.

According to the terms of settlement, petitioner no.1 is to pay to respondent no.2 a sum of Rs.9,50,000/- towards all her claims, including stridhan, jewellery, maintenance (past, present and future), alimony, etc.

sentences.text: 4. According to learned counsel, the entire sum of Rs.9,50,000/- has been tendered to respondent no.2.
Learned counsel for respondent no.2, on instructions of respondent no.2 who is present in person, confirms the receipt of the aforesaid amount.
5. It is also submitted that the parties, according to the terms of settlement, have also dissolved their marriage by way of decree of divorce under the provisions of Section 13B HMA, 1955.

The certified copy of the decree dated 28.04.2022 is placed on record, which was filed under the Index No.
1254361.
6.
IO is present in Court who identifies the parties, who are present in person.
7. This Court has interacted with respondent no.2, who affirms the terms of settlement.
She also confirms the receipt of Rs.9,50,000/- as full and final settlement and submits that she has no objection in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
8. This Court has perused the terms of settlement agreement and they appear to be lawful.
The parties are bound by the terms of the settlement.
9. After observing that the disputes are arising from matrimonial This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 00:08:32 ties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served in continuing with the FIR in question and the further criminal proceedings and it would be in the interest of justice as also of the parties and the society that quietus is put to such disputes.
10.
Accordingly, FIR No. 342/2019 dated 17.07.2019 under Sections 498A/406/34, IPC, registered at Police Station Dwarka South, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. The petition stands disposed of.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J OCTOBER 18, 2023 Aj
